pinterest.title: Wedding Photo App Guide: Collect Your Guests' Candid Photos in One Private Album
pinterest.description: Your photographer captures the vows and portraits. Your guests capture everything else. A wedding photo app gathers their photos and videos in one private album you control, alongside your photographer's gallery rather than instead of it. Compare shared album apps, QR code upload pages, disposable camera style apps, live slideshow displays and your photographer's own gallery, and see what to check before you choose.

pinterest.title: QR Code Wedding Photo Sharing: How to Set Up Guest Uploads on the Day
pinterest.description: Place a small QR card on every table and a larger one at the entrance beside the seating chart, where every guest pauses. Match the cards to your stationery and test every code on several phones. A browser upload page means guests can add photos with nothing to install, which suits grandparents and international guests alike. Mention it on your invitation and wedding website, and have the MC point guests to the cards at the reception.

pinterest.title: After the Wedding: How to Download, Back Up and Share Your Guest Photos
pinterest.description: Leave your wedding photo sharing album open for a few weeks for late uploads. Then download everything at full resolution, keep two copies in different places, and share a curated selection, minus anything a guest asked you to remove. Before you choose a tool, ask how long the album stays online, whether video is supported and whether you can download the full collection in one go.

slides: Your photographer captures the vows. Your guests capture everything else. Here is how to gather it all in one private album.
A wedding photo app collects your guests' photos and videos in one private album you control, alongside your photographer's gallery, never instead of it.
Five types to consider: shared album apps, QR code upload pages with no install, disposable camera style apps, live slideshow displays and your photographer's own gallery.
Before you choose, ask about browser uploads with no install, full resolution, video, moderation, a full download at the end, how long photos are kept and offline uploads.
Privacy first: ask guests before their photos are shared publicly, check with parents before sharing images of children, and remove any photo a guest asks you to take down.
On the day: a QR card on every table and a larger one at the entrance. Consider an unplugged ceremony, then invite uploads at the reception.
Marrying overseas? Ask the venue about Wi-Fi and data early, and choose a set-up that lets guests upload later from home.
Planning a destination wedding? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Your photographer will capture the vows, the portraits and the first dance. Your guests will capture everything else: the aunt who cried at the aisle, the groomsmen at the bar, the view from the back table as the sun went down.

A wedding photo app gathers those pictures and videos in one private place, so they don't scatter across phones and group chats. Our new guide recommends no specific apps. Instead, it covers:
- The main types: shared album apps, QR code upload pages, disposable camera style apps, live slideshow displays and your photographer's own gallery.
- What to check: total cost and what is included, browser uploads with no install, full resolution, video, moderation, a full download at the end, how long photos are kept and offline uploads.
- Privacy: ask guests before their photos are shared publicly, check with parents before sharing images of children, and remove any photo a guest asks you to take down.
- Set-up: a line on your invitation and wedding website, QR cards on tables and at the entrance, then download and back up everything afterwards.

A line on your welcome sign does a lot of work: please ask before sharing anyone else's photo publicly, and we will remove any picture on request.

Marrying overseas, where Wi-Fi is never a given? Ask the venue about internet and data early, and choose a set-up that lets guests upload later from home.

Planning a destination wedding? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
